summary_md: **Artificial Intelligence Papers ([@SciFi](https://x.com/SciFi/status/2115928883669213502))** shares *Free to Look, Free to Reason* ([arXiv 2610.35767](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35767)), which finds simple harnesses that let a capable model investigate (one call over an evidence package, a SQL agent, or the Codex agent) beat five hand-crafted root-cause-analysis agents on 90 validated cases across six models.

relevance: Evidence that simple harnesses can beat elaborate agent designs.

media.description: Image of the paper's abstract text.
media.ocr_text: Root cause analysis (RCA) of microservice failures has attracted many LLM agents whose investigation is hand-crafted, through standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents. Each is evaluated on its own data against few baselines, so it is unknown whether this design beats letting a capable model investigate on its own. We compare three simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls (one call over an evidence package, a SQL agent and the Codex coding agent) with five published LLM RCA agents and with statistical and causal methods on RCAtlas, 90 validated cases from eight public datasets, across six models and three reasoning efforts. The simple harnesses are the most accurate (PR@1 65-77% on three mid-tier models), ahead of the published agents (16-53%) and the non-LLM methods (6-39%), on every model on which both families were run.
